The Beta-Binomial Derivatives From the Direct Sums

Source: R/betabinom2_distrib.R
betabinom_direct.Rd

Returns the derivatives of one order of the beta-binomial log-mass from the finite sums over the integer shifts that the compiled kernel betabinom_direct_cpp forms, keyed as deriv_names() keys them. In the shapes \((\alpha, \beta)\) a pure derivative of order \(K\) in \(\alpha\) is \(c_K[\sum_{i<y}(\alpha+i)^{-K} - \sum_{i<n}(\alpha+\beta+i)^{-K}]\) with \(c_K = (-1)^{K-1}(K-1)!\), the pure one in \(\beta\) the same with \(n - y\), and a mixed one \(-c_K\sum_{i<n}(\alpha+\beta+i)^{-K}\). In the mean and dispersion \((\mu, \sigma)\) the sums run over \(\mu + i\sigma\), \(1 - \mu + i\sigma\) and \(1 + i\sigma\), with the power \(i^b\) for \(b\) derivatives in \(\sigma\). Every sum has terms of one sign, so the values keep their accuracy at any concentration; the cost is \(O(n)\) an observation.

Usage

betabinom_direct(y, p1, p2, n, order, params, shapes)

Arguments

y

A numeric vector of counts in \(\{0, \dots, n\}\).

p1, p2

The two parameters, mu and sigma or alpha and beta, each a numeric vector of length 1 or of the length of y.

n

The size, a single positive integer.

order

The derivative order, an integer from 1 to 4.

params

The names of the two parameters.

shapes

Logical of length 1: TRUE for the shapes, FALSE for the mean and dispersion.

Value

A named list of numeric vectors, one per distinct multi-index of the order, each of the length of the recycled inputs.

See also

bb_direct_cut() for where the families take this route; betabinom2_derivs() and betabinom1_components(), which call it.
